ferramentas.name: listAddresses
ferramentas.description: Returns all active delivery addresses on the user's account with usage analytics. **Always call this FIRST in any purchase flow** — it determines whether to confirm an existing address, let the user choose among saved addresses, or collect a new one. The chosen address must be the **exact** place where delivery should occur. Use the behavioral fields on each address (isLastUsedAddress, isMostUsedAddress30d, topMerchantTypes, topWeekDayShift, ordersByMerchantTypeWeekdayAndShift) to infer the most likely delivery address when multiple addresses are saved. When only one address is saved, use it directly and inform the user — no confirmation needed. When multiple addresses are saved, confirm briefly with the user (e.g., 'Entregar na Casa?') instead of listing all saved addresses. Only present the full list when behavioral data is unavailable, when signals are ambiguous, or when the user rejects or asks for alternatives. When an address has an alias ("Casa" or "Trabalho"), prefer presenting it by alias rather than the full street address. If no address is returned, guide the user to provide a new delivery address and use `createAddress` to save it. Do not construct or guess an addressId from address text. Only use the addressId values returned by this tool or by `createAddress`. Do **not** use this tool to search for new places or to save new addresses (use `createAddress`).

ferramentas.name: browseOffers
ferramentas.description: Browse what is available in an iFood business unit for the user's location. Use when the user wants to see what exists nearby, navigate the inventory, or discover available categories (e.g.: 'what's near me?', 'show me pet shop options', 'I want Japanese restaurants', 'show me desserts'). If there is a specific descriptive term (item, brand, attributes), prefer `searchOffers`. If the intent is personalised (favourites, reorder, recommendations), prefer `getRecommendations`. Canonical pattern: (1) open call with only merchantType + resultKind to get the full taxonomy tree in facets.itemTaxonomy; (2) drill-down with refinements.itemTaxonomy using canonical IDs from facets — never invent taxonomy IDs. Side effects: none (read-only).

ferramentas.name: getItem
ferramentas.description: Returns the full detail of a specific item: variants and complements (`customizations`), curated attributes (dietary, allergens, descriptors), promotions at item level, and a summary of the merchant that sells it. Use after the user has chosen or confirmed a specific item from a listing result. Do not use this tool to list or search items — use `browseOffers` or `searchOffers` for that. Items currently unavailable are not returned; an invalid or unavailable `itemId` yields an actionable error. Side effects: none (read-only).

ferramentas.name: getMerchant
ferramentas.description: Returns the full operational detail of a specific merchant: operating hours, all available delivery methods, supported payment methods, minimum order amount, rating, catalogue summary, and optionally featured items. Use after the user has chosen or confirmed a merchant from a listing result. Do not use this tool to list or search merchants — use `browseOffers` or `searchOffers` for that. Side effects: none (read-only).

Do not use when the user has a specific search term — prefer `searchOffers`. Do not use for generic browsing — prefer `browseOffers`. Side effects: none (read-only).

Decompose the utterance: the descriptive part goes in `query`; qualifiers like price, distance, fee, or rating go in `refinements`. Do not use this tool if there is no descriptive text — prefer `browseOffers` (browsing) or `getRecommendations` (personalization). Side effects: none (read-only).

ferramentas.name: listVouchers
ferramentas.description: Lists the vouchers available for the cart. Call this when the user wants to see which coupons or promo codes they can apply.

ferramentas.name: setVoucher
ferramentas.description: Applies a voucher or discount code to the cart. Call this when the user wants to apply a coupon or promo code they selected. Use a code and campaignId returned by the listVouchers tool.
